_comment: Per-surface capability matrix for the prompt interception kernel.
The hook runtimes and registration variants do NOT share one capability set,
supports every governance action. This file is the single place that records
what each surface can actually do, so the engine renders the correct shape
instead of emitting a field the runtime silently ignores. A hook that writes
an unsupported field does not fail loudly — the prompt simply goes to the
model ungoverned, which is the worst possible failure for a control.
Verified against vendor documentation on 2026-08-13. The hooks APIs on all
represented surfaces are Preview. Re-verify at each pilot checkpoint and bump
events        Event names this surface sends to the engine.
notifyOnly    Events that cannot change anything; log telemetry and exit.
promptField   stdin field holding the text to govern.
rewriteField  stdout field that REPLACES the model-facing prompt, or null.
injectField   stdout field that ADDS context beside the prompt, or null.
block         How a deliberate policy deny is expressed: 'decision',
'exit2', or null when the surface cannot block at all.
systemMessage Whether a 'systemMessage' string is surfaced to the developer.

github-sdk-user-prompt-submitted.notes: modifiedPrompt is honored only here; the hook itself cannot hard-reject, so a supported application must gate before session.send().

github-config-user-prompt-submitted.notes: Command and HTTP output is dropped, including modifiedPrompt; the lighter hosted/steering cloud runtime also ignores it.

github-user-prompt-transformed.notes: modifiedTransformedPrompt replaces model-facing content and session history but cannot block or handle the turn.

github-cloud-agent-policy-hooks.notes: Machine-wide policy hooks are Copilot CLI-only; cloud-agent hook behavior must be proven separately in the repository sandbox.

vscode.label: VS Code Copilot

deliveryProof.scope: VS Code UserPromptSubmit additionalContext on the tested local client; revalidation required after upgrades

notes: additionalContext CONFIRMED 2026-08-09: live VS Code session with the hook
active received the governance block and the model followed the governed
security-fix workflow unprompted — searched for instruction anchors, applied
parameterized SQL, added a regression test, flagged for human review.
modifiedPrompt is still unverified: VS Code documents no prompt-replacement
field on UserPromptSubmit. The engine emits modifiedPrompt speculatively but
governance does NOT depend on it. Do not describe this surface as 'rewriting'
prompts until rewriteVerified is true.
permissionDecision/permissionDecisionReason are PreToolUse-only and are
ignored here, so exit 2 is the only documented way to stop a prompt.

claude.label: Claude Code

deliveryProof.scope: Vendor contract is represented; an end-to-end model-receipt canary has not been recorded

notes: Claude Code cannot replace prompt text on any event; the documentation is
explicit that UserPromptSubmit 'can't replace the prompt; it only injects
additionalContext alongside it'. UserPromptExpansion cannot rewrite either.
Blocking is the top-level {"decision":"block","reason":...} form, NOT
permissionDecision. UserPromptSubmit takes no matcher and lowers the
default command timeout to 30s.

copilot-sdk.label: Copilot SDK programmatic hook

deliveryProof.scope: Official SDK contract only; no pinned SDK application or downstream model-receipt canary is recorded

notes: modifiedPrompt is honored only for an SDK programmatic hook.
The hook cannot hard-reject a prompt. Applications claiming pre-send
prevention must enforce the decision before calling session.send().
This adapter is a wire-contract implementation and is not distributed
as a command hook because command/HTTP output is dropped.

copilot-cli.label: Copilot CLI / coding agent

deliveryProof.scope: userPromptTransformed mutation is documented; a pinned-runtime downstream canary has not been recorded

notes: userPromptSubmitted command/HTTP output is dropped, including
modifiedPrompt, so the configured command hook is telemetry-only.
userPromptTransformed is mutation-only: it can rewrite what the model
receives but cannot block. An enforcing deny rule therefore CANNOT stop a
prompt here — it degrades to a hard refusal instruction written into the
rewritten prompt. That is a genuine enforcement gap, not parity.
The composer replaces transformed content with a governed envelope that
contains the available original prompt exactly once and verifies it locally.
